utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Repic, I'd like to remind you that you're still -- first, Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Repic, I first -- I'd forgotten to have the case called. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Repic, I was asking you some questions yesterday afternoon about your knowledge or otherwise of the involvement of PJP forces in the incident on the 5th of March at the Decane compound in Prekaz and on the 28th of February and the 1st of March on the villages of Likoshan and Qirez. Can I ask you please again in relation to the 5th of March operation on Prekaz, having had an opportunity to reflect on it overnight, were PJP officers involved in that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to reply in the negative again. In the -- I did not take part in the operation or in its preparations. My duty was to take over duty at the factory for hunting ammunition, to take over from my colleagues. Now, as to whether they had participated in that operation, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is the thing I want to probe with you, Mr. Repic, which surely arriving in that area where the PJP forces had been stationed, 10 days after the incident at Prekaz, you would have discussed that incident with the colleagues that you were replacing or relieving, would you not?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember those discussions. I can just briefly convey to you the official information that was given to us when we took over.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if it answers the question I'm asking you, then please do.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have told you yesterday in my evidence, we had to prepare our unit for deployment before we arrived in the area of Kosovska Mitrovica, so we received official information that we were to relieve the unit in the area of Srbica, in the hunting ammunition factory, which had held those positions, securing the factory, and some other positions around Srbica itself. We were also told that in the Jashari Mahala, there had been an armed clash after Adem Jashari and other male members of his family resisted arrest that was attempted by police. Now, as to who participated in that operation, I truly don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And so far as Likoshan and were concerned, the operations that had taken place a week before, what was the position there? Did you know whether PJP forces had been involved in those operations?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you a passage from a judgement of another Trial Chamber of this Tribunal in respect of those incidents and invite you to comment on your knowledge of what is there recorded. I'll read it to you slowly so it can be translated. This is paragraph 49 from the Limaj judgement. "On the 28th of February and the 1st of March 1998, Serbian police forces launched an attack on the villages of Qirez and Likoshan located two kilometres apart in the Drenica area. Helicopters, armoured military vehicles, mortars and machine-guns were used in the attack. In both cases, the Serbian Special Police forces attacked without a warning and fired indiscriminately at civilians. "On or about the 5th of March, Serbian security forces attacked the family compound of the leader of the KLA Adem Jashari in Prekazi i Poshtem, a village located not far from Likoshan and Qirez also in the area of Drenica. The fighting in which armoured vehicles were used continued for about 36 hours. The evidence is that during the February-March 1998 attacks in the area of Drenica, 83 Kosovar Albanians were killed. Among the dead victims were elderly people as well as at least 24 women and children. During the attack on Qirez a pregnant woman was shot in the face and a baby was killed in Prekazi i Poshtem. Many of the victims were shot at very close range. Reports indicated men were summarily executed in front of their homes and that some of the victims were shot dead while in police custody. During the attack on Prekaz, the entire Jashari family except for an 11-year-old girl was killed." What I want to ask you is was there an investigation taking place into the legality and propriety of the police actions on those dates when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was any effort made to identify and isolate the Special Police forces that had taken part in those operations?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to emphasise again that I commanded a company. What you are asking me goes beyond my scope of work or knowledge. Perhaps this looks odd to you, but concerning these things that you're asking me about, whether there were investigations, whether participants were identified and so on, I truly don't know about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You presumably then don't know whether any disciplinary action was taken against any of the Special Police forces involved?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me move on, then, please, to your transfer to Junik in mid-May. Just before I do, just give me one moment. You told us that there were other PJP units stationed in the area to the west of the main Pec-to-Gjakove road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that. I don't know what is the context that you took it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you again in case I've misunderstood your testimony. When you arrived in mid-May in Junik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you please refer to the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I find the reference and provide it to Your Honours later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you again. When you arrived in Junik in mid-May you were relieving an existing PJP contingent that was there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were there other PJP contingents stationed on the west of the main Pec-to-Gjakove road, for example in the area around Penosvac, at the time that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you caught me by surprise a bit. It's difficult for me to create a picture in my head about the location, but let me give you an explanation to the extent that I can. There were other forces in that area stationed in that area around Decane, in Pec, in Djakovica. There were units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn to tab 9 in the red file for a moment, please? And whilst that's being done, the reference that Your Honour asked for, I believe, is 8489, line 15. It may be that it's to some extent overtaken by the witness's answers more recently. The document that you are looking at, Mr. Repic, is a situation report filed by the office of the British military attache to Belgrade following a visit to Penosvac, which as you will recall is south of Junik on the west side of the road on the 11th and 12th of May and it begins by recording that "The situation in Penosvac area is very tense, the area of Penosvac, Djakovica, Pec and Decane are patrolled by elements of the JSO and the PJP in a very heavy-handed way. Villagers have fled north to Junik." That's the summary, and then in paragraph 2 under the heading detail, it reads, "Penosvac, roads south to Penosvac carpeted in empty cases including 40-millimetre grenades, villages south of Penosvac deserted, live-stock slaughtered in fields, houses sprayed with gunfire, Penosvac empty, except for JSO/PJP who are carrying out patrols from Decane using APCs," that's armoured personnel carriers, "including TABC 79 and IPR similar to M-60. Most villagers now concentrated in Junik, about 300 with enough food and water but no telephone." And then finally under the heading assessment in paragraph 7 on the following page, the reporter records, "Heavy-handed terror action in Penosvac area indicates that the tactical thought process has not changed." That is a reference to the tactical thought process of the Serbian forces deployed there, Mr. Repic. Now, you arrived, I think you said, in the second half of May. Were you aware that there had been an operation to the south of Junik in which JSO and PJP forces had slaughtered live-stock, sprayed houses with gunfire and caused the civilian population to flee northwards towards Junik?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for there being operations in the area that you mentioned, yes, we were informed about that. But we were not told about all of the details, exact descriptions, consequences and the description that you gave us. We were not told about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before he goes on can I just simply ask that the record reflect that the exhibit was I think D110 which the witness is being shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I asked you yesterday as to whether you were aware of Serbian Special Police forces shooting live-stock, burning haystacks, making areas uninhabitable. When you arrived, was any of the detailed information about the operation that had been taking place south of Junik conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand, in both of these instances, both when you arrived in Prekaz or while, I'm sorry, in Srbica 10 days after Prekaz -- the Prekaz incident and when you arrive in Junik 10 days after the operation that's here described, in each instance, you told us there is a process of you relieving forces that are there in a handover but in neither instance are you given any detailed briefing of what's been taking place in the fortnight before you arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to clarify that the handover of duty between the two units does not include a detailed discussion and briefing at the level of company commanders about the activities that had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, may I then turn to the operation that you described as having begun on the 25th of May following first of all the disappearance of Mr. Popadic and Mr. Jovanovic and then the attack involving Milutin Novakovic? In your witness statement in this case, you indicate that on the 24th of March -- I'm sorry, I apologise, "On the 25th of May, 1998, PJP units, I believe from Djakovica, started searching for our missing colleagues in the villages in the area, specifically in the area along the villages Babaloc and Junik towards Prilep." And you described that yesterday in your testimony as an operation comprising special measures to sweep the terrain. I wonder, can you just help us in a little bit more detail about that operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, would it not be appropriate to have the statement introduced? Because it's not in evidence, that the witness gave the statement. I take it that you're referring to the 15th of December 2006 statement. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you first ask the witness whether he has given such a statement because I don't think it has been mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You gave a statement in this matter to the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in that statement, you mentioned the 25th of May operation that you told us about in your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was your company involved in that sweep?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But other PJP companies were involved?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you if I may about two matters in connection with events on or around the 25th of May. Human rights organisations have reported that during the week of the 25th of May, many of the villages from Pec to Gjakove were shelled whilst civilians were present. Can I ask you, please, were you aware that shelling was taking place?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not quite clear to me. Which villages and what do you mean by shelling? Artillery shelling or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can help us. From your own recollection during that operation that you described, was there artillery shelling on villages in the area?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Was there any other form of grenades used to attack villages in the area on the week of the 25th of May as part of that sweep?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again you're asking me about something where I did not participate myself. I do not exclude the possibility that hand-held rocket launchers were used or perhaps hand-grenades. This was an operation that included sweeping of the terrain, so that possibility is there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we understand, then, in that context, you recognise that sweeping of the terrain is something that could include rocket launchers and grenades. What is the object of sweeping? What does the word "sweeping" mean in this context?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sweeping of the terrain is the equivalent of the police term "search of the terrain." The purpose of that operation was to locate the two policemen who had gone missing as well as the motor vehicle in which they had been travelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there, as a result of this operation, a situation in which many of the villagers left their villages because they were under attack from Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of whether they had left their villages but one of the consequences of such operations is definitely fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, human rights organisations have recorded as part of the activity in the week of the 25th of May that non-combatants fleeing their villages were shot at by Serbian forces. Is that something that you have any knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that after that operation, many villages were systematically destroyed and live-stock shot to ensure that nobody could return in the short run.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you now, please, to turn to tab 10 in the red bundle, which, for the record, is Exhibit P6 at page 23 of the exhibit. This is another incident that took place on the 25th of May in the village of Ljubenic which is on the Pec-to-Decane stretch of the road and it records, and I'll just read two short passages into the record so that it can be translated for you. "On the basis of its research into the events at Ljubenic village near Pec in Kosovo, the humanitarian law centre has established that at least five ethnic Albanians were killed on the 25th of May 1998. All the victims were men whose ages ranged from 23 to 68, all were members of the Hamzaj family and were killed in their homes. The bodies were found in the yard shared by the Hamzaj family dressed only in underwear and with visible marks of torture. Two houses were destroyed and four burned." A little further down is a description of those involved in the operation. "Around 1.30 p.m., the same day, a 250 to 300-strong police unit arrived in Ljubenic from the direction of Stellc village in trucks, buses, four-wheel drives and several armoured personnel carriers. The police were equipped and armed for action in the field. They entered the village after first subjecting it to heavy artillery and small-arms fire. Some of the police were bearded, which indicates that they were not regular members of the force. The artillery and small-arms fire which lasted for over an hour was heard by an HLC researcher who was in the area at the time." Now, pausing there to let the translation catch up, before I ask you further questions about this, I wonder if you could turn behind tab 11, which is an extract from a report by the OSCE, and if you look at the second page of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's Exhibit D72, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the second page, it reads as follows: "Ljubenic just off the main road to Decane, seven kilometres south of Pec is a mixed village situated at the foot of steep cliffs rising high above the plain. It was the site of a reported mass killing on the 25th of May 1998 in which eight people were extrajudicially executed by the Serbian police. At that time, independent verifiers were unable to reach this area of heavy fighting. During fighting which began a few days later, about 40 houses were destroyed or severely damaged, with most of the Kosovar Albanian population moved out." And you'll see, Mr. Repic, there is a footnote there, footnote 88, to an Amnesty International report, and if you just flip through the photographs published at the time in Koha Ditore newspaper of the individuals who lost their lives in that incident are linked with the OSCE footnote 88. Now, I want to ask you about this aspect of the sweep operation. To your knowledge, what was the area covered by the sweep operation that you described on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, that operation covered the area to the north of Junik, to the left side of the road if you look in the direction of Decane, and a part of the Rastavica village. I don't know how deep it went to the right side of the road. I can't tell you, because I did not participate in that action. But in the direction of Decane. As for the depth, whether they really went all the way up to Decane, I can't really tell you, but that would be the basic axis. As far as I can recall, that's what I can confirm on the basis of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we've understood your testimony about the axis. Are you saying that the sweep operation entered the territory on both sides of the main road, although you don't know how far it went on either side?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on both sides of the road because the objective was to locate our colleagues and vehicles, so if you look at -- in the direction of Decane, it was on both sides of the road but I can't tell you the depth, how deep they went from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said earlier that given that it was a sweep operation, you wouldn't exclude the use of hand-held rocket launchers. I wonder if you could just explain to us how a hand-held rocket launcher might be used in a search operation.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hand-held rocket launchers are used in such actions to neutralise resistance points, and the resistant point is a bunker, a fortified house, a yard, a machine-gun emplacement, a place where their hand-held rocket launchers are firing from, a resistance point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know, then, where those resistance points were, that this fighting took place during that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about this incident in Ljubenic, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way that you put it to me, no, I didn't know about that. I knew that there were actions in that area too, as you said, to the south of Pec, but I was not aware of any events that were -- that developed in the way that you just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And those actions that you knew about that took place south of Pec, were they part of the same sweep operation?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you've told us you were aware of the actions. Just help us, if you can, were there two different operations going on on the 25th of May or was it part of one coordinated action? It's the same date, as you see, along the same road, albeit rather further north. You told us you knew about those operations towards Pec. Were they part of the same sweep operation?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood me when I -- when you say that I knew about the operation. I knew that units were active in that area, but as to when it was and whether it was a synchronised action, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I move on to a little later in time, just to have a sense of your knowledge of some other events? You had tours of duty in Kosovo up to and including the summer of 1999, I think you confirmed yesterday. Can you help us as to when during 1999 you were deployed in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just clarify, 1998 I was there just a couple of shifts, not the entire time from March until the end of the year. So that may have been a total of three or four months all together. As for 1999, we came there on the eve of the day when the air strikes began.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, again, bearing in mind that I'm asking you about your knowledge as widely as possible of police operations in this area at that time, about two events that took place in April of 1999, to see if you can help us with those at all? First of all, on the 1st and 2nd of April 1999, police action in the Qerim, that is Q-e-r-i-m, district of Gjakove resulted in the death of a significant number of women and children. In one instance, 25 people, at 163 Milos Gilic [phoen] Street. The victims, all but one of them, were female and included nine children under ten years of age. Were you aware of the police action in Gjakove at the beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the question. Unless Mr. Emmerson is putting it as a matter of credit to this witness, the Prosecution submits that it is not relevant to the indictment of the matters before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, the Chamber noticed that you, in let's say going in the direction of finding out whether the witness had some knowledge, that you covered a lot of details, of course very cruel details, of matters that happened. And then we would hear from the witness that he wasn't aware of that, so therefore if we do it the other way around, if you give a short description of the event and then first find out whether the witness has any knowledge of it and go into any further details if he has. If he has not, then of course there is another matter, the relevance of what happened in 1999. I didn't stop you but of course it's in time far away from the indictment. So therefore come to your point quickly, or otherwise, we have to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Repic? Do you know of any police operations in Gjakove during April, the first part of April 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was in Kosovska Mitrovica, and I did not know about those actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, then, please, towards the other end of the month, were you -- or where were you stationed in the end -- at the end of April?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, in April, we spent most of our time in the Kosovska Mitrovica area or rather Srbica. It is likely that I was in Srbica during April too. I assume that I was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just put one matter to you and if there is an objection, please pause before you reply. On or about the 27th of April, a large number of men were detained and killed by a joint police and army operation in the village of Maja and their bodies were subsequently discovered in an SAJ barracks in Batajnica, in Serbia, in 2001 and 2002. Is that something that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to that. It's going way beyond any attack on the witness's credibility. If Mr. Emmerson had the information necessary to impeach the witness by suggesting that he participated in attacks on civilians in April 1999, he would have put it to the witness by now. This is going way beyond a fishing expedition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The mere fact whether a witness was aware of that is not something that would assist the Chamber. Of course, if there would-- if you want to suggest that there was any involvement of the witness, then of course it would be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm, A, not in a position to and, B, not suggesting that the witness was involved in either of those operations, nor am I asking these questions as matters going to credit. I'm asking these questions to determine whether the witness is in a position to shed any light on events which involved tactical operations by the Serbian Special Police forces and that is material which we would be eliciting with a view to giving the Trial Chamber a picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you're seeking as a matter of fact is whether -- not only whether the witness is aware of something of the kind that may have happened, but also whether he had any insider knowledge and anything more than just hearing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll be directed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll allow that question and then we move on. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that something you were aware of, Mr. Repic, or are aware of now?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Can I ask you, please, to confirm that Mr. Popadic and Mr. Jovanovic were armed with automatic weapons at the time when they disappeared?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were armed with side-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, they were armed, were they not, with an M-70 automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: M-99 or TZ-99 pistol, and the automatic rifle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. There's just one other area I want to explore with you, please, and I wonder if for this purpose you could be handed a small additional bundle and perhaps the Trial Chamber might have it as well, and in order to deal with this, I need to give the Trial Chamber a very brief explanation of what it is we are looking at here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to do that when the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy for the witness to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This follows on from the questions that Mr. Re asked about the form of statements amongst documents that are retrieved from 65 ter 1973, which he yesterday asked the witness to identify by reference to their form. Can I indicate what it is that one sees in this file?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Repic, if you just bear with me for a moment, please. Item number 2 is Exhibit P390, the statement purportedly made by Zenelj Alija which we have seen before and which has been introduced into evidence in another context. Item number 1 -- I'm sorry, I do apologise, item number 2 is a statement made by Bekim Kalamashi. Item number 1 is the same statement as it an appears in the file that Mr. Re took the witness to yesterday and one has the same pattern for three and four. Item number 4 is Exhibit P871 as previously exhibited. Item number 3 is the same statement as it appears in the file, 65 ter number 1973. And I just want you to help us, if you can, please, Mr. Repic, because you've been asked some questions about the form of statements. If you look at statement number 1, first of all, and statement number 2, you can see, I think, from a very brief glance, that it is the same document. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me if this statement tallies with the other statement that I looked at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm asking you whether the statement behind tab 1 and the statement behind tab 2 are obviously the same document? Let me just help you a little, if I may. If you look at the statement behind tab 1, just below halfway down the statement, you can find a paragraph that begins with the word, "Nedelju," N-e-d-e-l-j-u. If you look at the last word in that statement, you can see that there has been overtyping. Do you see that? Two letters in the last word of that paragraph have been overtyped. Mr. Repic, I'm interrupting you because I can see you're looking at the wrong part of the statement. Just bear with me for a moment. If you look at the first page of the statement behind tab 1, about halfway down there is a paragraph that begins "Nedelju." Do you see that paragraph, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you look at the very last word of that paragraph, can you see there is overtyping on it? Two letters that have been overtyped. Do you see that? Just four our five lines down there is a line that begins "Raspolzivi" and the last two letters on that line have been overtyped. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please help me, the available assets to the last drop of our blood? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about content but purely about form. Can you see the paragraph beginning "Nedelju"?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look five lines down, there is a line that begins "Raspolzivi." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now look to the end of that line. It reads "Krivi" and then there is a word that has been overtyped, two letters. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you just look over the page, please, to page 2 of the statement, you can see, if you would, please, just to look at the second-to-last line of the text and the very last word there, you see that that has also been overtyped with three Xs. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just look to the statement behind tab 2, you can confirm, please, for the record, that those two overtyping errors are also replicated in the statement behind tab 2 in exactly the same positions. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on page 1 and page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, one difference between these two documents is that the document behind tab 2 has a stamp on it. Do you see that? Whereas the document behind tab 1 has no stamp on it.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, purely on the basis of form, was it the practice to put stamps on a document after it was signed in that way?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Documents are verified by stamps, those documents that are sent out. But those documents that are filed in the archives, they are not stamped. That's -- that is the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So one would go to the archive and one would be sent out and that might explain why one is stamped and the other isn't? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Looking at the document behind tab 2, the one that was stamped, can you see the date is the 3rd of September 1998? It's at the top of the statement, Mr. Repic. Mr. Repic, it's at the very beginning of the statement. Top of the first page you'll find the date. I think you're looking at the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: On the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Top left side. You see the date is the 3rd of September?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says the 3rd of September in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the document behind tab 1, which in all other respects apart from the stamp is identical, can you have a look for us at the date on that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell whether anything was altered here, the 13, 14, I really can't see it. It's very unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, yesterday some questions were put to the witness in asking him about the format of documents, and of course the format reflects the ordinary. So therefore the Chamber is wondering where you're heading for. It may be clear that at least the Chamber understood that it's the position of the Defence that these are results of manipulation and et cetera, et cetera. And of course format questions and format knowledge would not be of a kind to reveal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honour's hands. I don't want to pursue it -- I've pursued it with this witness because it comes from the same exhibit as the documents that Mr. Re elicited from the witness yesterday but I'm happy to take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you understand that if you're heading for, if you just want to look at the format, but from all your questions now it seems that you are drawing the attention of the witness to differences and et cetera, and if you just stay with the format, I'm fine but if you want to -- if you're seeking any explanations on possible inconsistencies or possible manipulations, then of course we would first have to know whether the witness has any knowledge of the creation of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we've already established that the witness does not know the contents of the file, so I won't proceed in that way. But may I ask, please, that the documents behind tab 1 and tab 3 be marked for identification. And may I simply invite the Trial Chamber, then, in those circumstances, to note that there has plainly been in respect of both sets of documents an alteration of the date by the insertion or deletion of 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Mr. Emmerson waits, we can very quickly - Ms. Schweiger is trying to find the information now - inform the Trial Chamber when we received the two documents and which sources they've come from. I suspect they've come from two different requests for assistance from the Serbian authorities and were pursued at the different times. I don't know but we're checking. I can easily put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least some questions were put to the witness in respect of that. Without expressing any view of the Chamber at this moment as to the probative value and -- but marking for identification is not a problem. Mr. Registrar, would you then the first one being 65 ter number 1973 page 27.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this will be marked for identification as D163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And then the other one is 65 ter same number, 1973, page 29 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Marked for identification as D164, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Isn't that already P390, according to the index the Defence has supplied?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not? It's behind tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We are now talking about tab 1 and tab 3, where 390 is behind tab 2. That's at least what the Defence has indicated. That's what I find in the index in the beginning of -- oh, no. I made a mistake as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think I'm right, yes. We find exhibit numbers behind tab 2 introduced -- indicates which witness. Okay. Let's proceed. If you want to revisit the matter, Mr. Re, please come back to it. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith? Mr. Repic, Mr. Guy-Smith is counsel, Defence counsel for Mr. Balaj and he'll now cross-examine you. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have but a few questions, Mr. Repic. During the time that you were in Kosovo in May, was there a check-point at Dolovo manned by Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with Dolovo at all. I don't know whether there was a check-point. I don't even know where that settlement is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, do you recall where the Serbian check-points were on the road between where you were stationed at Junik and Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only remember the check-point at the entrance into Djakovica, the outskirts, and I don't remember others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As part of your responsibility as commander of the special unit that you have told us about, were you in radio communication with those check-points?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had a local radios, and whenever needed we would contact the seat of the Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As part of your responsibility as commander, did you file daily reports concerning your activities and contacts with either the civilian population or, as you have termed them, armed Albanians?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We reported -- the staff -- we reported to the staff, briefed the staff every morning and the staff was located at the Secretariat headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were the briefings that you engaged in every morning briefings that were ultimately memorialised so that there is a record of those briefings that you had a chance to review?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually not aware of whether anything was written down from our reports and whether -- and if so, whether such documents were archived. We conveyed our information either via radios or telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And specifically, as commander, when you conveyed information, who did you convey information to? Was there a particular individual who you were responsible to convey information to?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These daily reports were made by duty officers in units, and they were conveyed to duty officers at the Secretariats. What I personally did was make reports or briefings on weekly basis or so, and I informed the head of the Secretariat and commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you could, the head of the Secretariat that you informed on a weekly basis was who?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was a person whose last name was Adamovic. I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the commander of the detachment that you made these weekly reports to, who was that?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Branko Prljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have occasion, in your capacity as commander, to double check the daily reports that were sent out by the duty officer as to make sure that the information that was being sent out was accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the information conveyed by my duty officer to the duty officer at the Secretariat?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information conveyed by duty officer was the information that we compiled based on the briefings every morning, and I explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the briefings every morning included whatever activities that your unit engaged in during the previous day, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that your unit was stationed at Junik and at Babaloc, were you wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those uniforms were what kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniforms of the PJP were camouflage uniforms with grey colours in different -- different shades of grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was it the responsibility of the people in your unit to maintain their uniforms? And by that, I mean to be dressed in uniforms during the time that they were on duty, while they were stationed at Junik and Babaloc?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They did have duty to maintain their uniforms. We had inspections every morning, inspections of our members, and they had to maintain their uniforms, unless they were on a special task, such as the case of Rade Popadic and Jovanovic who had been sent out to get food. They were sent out in civilian clothes, and in a civilian vehicle, in order to be as inconspicuous as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand what you've said in that regard, sir. When these two gentlemen returned and were in the process of unloading which you've told us about, were you present during that unloading of the food?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, they made it only as far as Babaloc. They didn't make it back to Junik and I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that their colleagues assisted them in unloading the food at Babaloc. Are the colleagues you're referring to other members of the special unit?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "other members of the special unit." They were all members of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. And what I'm asking you is when their colleagues were assisting them in unloading the food, those were members of your unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those men were, as you've told us, in uniform, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Repic, could you tell me, you told us that you were a commander of a company. Did I understand well that this is approximately 150 men, 100 of them located near Babaloc, 50 located near Junik? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A company has up to 150 people. I don't remember exactly what our strength was during that particular shift. There were about 42 or 43 men in Junik and the rest were in Babaloc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know what the strength of the PJP forces was in the villages around or the, for example, in Gjakove or in Decan or -- do you have any idea on how many PJP --

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the villages nearby? Could you tell us whether there were PJP units -- I do understand you came to assist the local PJP units. What was the Junik PJP strength before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it five or 15 or 70 or could you give us any impression on the approximate strength of the local units?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about local forces? The ones that we came to relieve -- or to assist, rather?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, PJP forces, Special Police forces, not ordinary police but Special Police forces.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the local police, there was a squad there, which means that there were between five to eight men, local policemen. The unit we came to relieve was approximately same size, numerically speaking, as we were. I couldn't tell you how many men they had exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that the unit of the same size was not a local unit but was also sent in from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they then -- you said the unit you came to relieve, did they stay so that you have the double strength at that moment?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We relieved them in shifts. We rotated, one shift came to relieve the other shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the ones who were there left for where?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only suppose where they went. Most likely they had gone back to their original Secretariats from which they had originally come. Now, as to they had any special tasks, I really don't know that. I'm making these assumptions because I know that this was a rotation, so I assume that they went back to their original Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm coming back to Gjakove. You had no idea about the strength of the local units. Do you mean the original units like the squad present in Junik or by any sent-in units, whether or not rotating with others?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no information as to the strength of the Secretariats -- rather local forces of the original Secretariat. Nor do I know how many people of the PJP units were sent to the Djakovica area in that particular period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was your area of responsibility geographically limited or what would be -- and if so, what would be the area where you would be responsible?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task during that shift was somewhat specific. We came there with our company to secure two refugee settlements. Our responsibilities extended to the refugee settlement in Junik and the one in Babaloc. That means that we were a stationary unit without any kind of tasks that would involve manoeuvres or movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that also explain why, in the sweeping the terrain operation, you were not involved? Because your task of your unit was a stationary one rather than an operational one?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We were a stationary unit and we only provided logistical support to the units who had come to take part in actions. When I say logistical support, that meant accommodation, ensuring that they had a safe base from which they could go out into operation and return to, where they could be provided with food and where they could stay safely when not in action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember how many refugees there were there in -- well, let's start with the Babaloc refugee centre.

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember is that those were the settlements they had about 100 houses, houses being the size of a one or two-room apartment with a bit of -- with a bit of land around it. Not all of the houses were inhabited. Based on that, I'm assuming that there were maybe up to 200 refugees in Babaloc, and Junik also had about 100 houses of the same size, with a bit of land attached to them and once again, not all of the houses were inhabited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said most of the people of your company went to Babaloc, and a lesser number to Junik. Is -- because you said that there were over 40 to Junik, a complete company would be up until 150. Would my calculation that there would be some 100 PJP people in Babaloc, would that be a correct one?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking myself, if you've got 100 houses with 200 refugees, is 100 PJP to secure the settlement, is that a normal size of-- for such a task?

utterances.speaker: RADE REPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you consider the situation that existed in Babaloc, then you may wonder why is it that two-thirds of the unit were stationed in Babaloc and one-third in Junik. At that time, Junik was still a village that had had no problems, no incidents. We went into Junik, we went on patrol duty with local policemen in Junik. We contacted residents. We visited Serbian houses on the outskirts of Junik. As for the provocations against residents and policemen in Babaloc were much more intense. They were much more intense. Because that village, neighbours much more difficult territory where there were first attempts to group, establish headquarters, and put civilians into uniforms. So if you look at that settlement, which is some 100 to 200 metres long, if you have to provide security and you have to put security detail that works in shifts, then that task requires approximately the number of policemen that you mentioned, that is to say between 90 and 100 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Re, any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, there is no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No need. Then if the questions of the Bench have not raised any need for further questions to Defence counsel, then, Mr. Repic, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming, it's quite a distance to come to The Hague, and for having answered questions of both parties and of the Bench, and I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any exhibits either tendered already or to be tendered and on which we would have to take a decision? Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 2, Your Honour, which is an order signed by Colonel Zivanovic which I put to this witness. Your Honour will recall it's the deep wedging of the documents dated the 8th of August and it is 65 ter number 1945.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was tab 2? Yes. Has that received a number? Not yet. Mr. Registrar that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D165, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D165 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Emmerson, anything else? Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The exhibits which I had marked for identification yesterday, I'm not pressing at this moment. We will return to those at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact we said we would wait until a later stage to see whether you would tender them. You did not tender them yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's just a timing matter. In terms of court time, I prefer not to argue the task now because we have another witness waiting but at some later pint we can return to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, it was my distinct understanding that Mr. Re had intended on calling another witness with regard to those documents and he was not planning on tendering them at all until another witness had been called so I'm not quite sure that the representation made at this point is accurate and I'm just trying to make sure that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, we'll wait and see when Mr. Re comes back to the issue and then we'll check carefully on the transcripts what he said when he said he would not tender them at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also what the Chamber then responded to that. That's on the record. Then of course, there is the other documents, the two marked for identification, Mr. Emmerson, do I understand you're not tendering them?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to tender them at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, of course, you are asking the Court to look at the differences which of course is -- which just marked for identification might be a problem but perhaps you could agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps I could reserve my position in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour will recall that there has been cross-examination in the past of witnesses who have given certain explanations in respect of that batch of documents, and at the time of that cross-examination took place we did not have available to us two other versions with different dates. It may be, I don't know yet, that there is yet a further witness to come who deals with that aspect of the case. There is certainly an individual who is on the Prosecution's witness list who deals with that aspect of the case, although I understand--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So these are new versions of, again, documents that look very similar. One of the things that came into my mind, not to be resolved at this moment but perhaps for the parties to look at, is whether carbon paper was used at the time, because sometimes differences on an original, if you type out a mistake, then they sometimes remain on the carbon. I'm not saying that this is an explanation but the Chamber of course, looking only at photocopies is not in a position to identify whether such a thing could have happened. I don't know, Mr. Re, to what extent these documents arrived as photocopies or whether in originals. It gives me the impression sometimes that carbon copies are used, which of course may complicate matters. May also provide on the circumstances an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll check it. I know we did receive some original documents recently from Serbian security which I think they gave us by accident instead of copies. Normally we just get copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- yes, of course, but the word "original" gets a very special meaning because carbon copies would then be originals to the extent that they are not photocopied again. This is just for the parties to keep this in the back of their mind. Positions are reserved, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll just indicate obviously if Your Honour has that thought in mind, the discrepancy between the two groups of documents on its face is the same. In other words, 10 days' difference between the two statements as regards both of the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was not seeking further comments on the documents at this moment. Then, Mr. Re, may I take it that after the break you're ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He's here and ready to testify and I assume outside waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we have a break first. We have a break and we'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dourel. Welcome in this hall of justice. If you will allow me, I will continue in English. [In English] Mr. Dourel, before you give evidence in this courtroom, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require to you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed out to you, I take it the French version, to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down. [In English] Mr. Dutertre, is it you who is going to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dourel, could you please confirm your identity? And first of all, I would like to ask a practical question. Please wait and look at the screen, the monitor, to see that the translation in English has stopped so that you can then answer. Mr. Dourel, therefore, your name is Laurent Dourel and you are French nationality?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you tell me where you were born?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: I am born in Albi in the department of Tarn in France and I am born on the 22 July 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to see your curriculum vitae and I would ask for Exhibit 1984 of list 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's part already of the -- is that part of the report that has been submitted, Mr. Dutertre? I'm just asking because if you're using 65 ter numbers, then I always have to ask myself whether it's already marked for identification or not. If you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible, Mr. President. It's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's the last two pages of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- no. I have a bibliography. I see the English version, last two pages is professional experience, et cetera, et cetera. But the French, I'm just wondering where to find that in the French version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't found it in the French version. Oh, yes. Number 1985 of list 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is it part of the submitted report? Then please, because I see annex A to the Prosecution's submissions of expert report of Laurent Dourel, annex A is the French version and that ends with ERN number 169776. Previous page is the -- is a letter dated the 25th of July, written by you, Mr. Dutertre, and addressed to Lieutenant Dourel and then the previous annex is a bibliography and then I come to the conclusion, whereas in the English version I found an annex -- oh, yes, I see it's annex C but then French and English together at the very end. Yes. Thank you. It's -- I take it that you wanted to put the curriculum to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President. We received several documents so that may explain the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Dourel, could you confirm that what you see on the screen is indeed your curriculum vitae, your CV?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So this is your name. I would like to delve on certain points to enlighten members of the Chamber. You are -- you are -- have a specialty, professionally, which is rather uncommon. What is exactly your training as an entomologist? I don't think it's -- it's probably the first time this happens. Could you indicate what is your specialty as a forensic entomologist?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes. I am deputy to the entomology department of the Institute of Criminal Research of the National Gendarmerie in France. Our goal is to do expertise work for magistrates or at the request of police in order to give a date or an estimated date thanks to the help of the insects found on corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you specify whether your specialty is a recent specialty or is it already something that has existed for some time?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: It's an old discipline, matter, which exists since 12th century but there is no university training in this specific subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I refer to your CV. You worked for one year at the IRCGN in 1997-98, and then you again with this institute in 2002. Could you tell us first of all when did the IRCGN was created and what is its role in general, institute of criminal research?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: The institute was created in 1987 and its present form in 1992, the IRCGN has four divisions in charge of criminal matters, criminal research, with 12 departments. Each of these departments, groups the whole of the criminal questions which may interest justice. So this institute has as a goal to do expertise work for the police and the magistrates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. How many people does the entomology of the institute count?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Five people in the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Including yourself?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that magistrates ask the institute for expertise in entomology matters. Could you specify whether the police has also a department for entomology?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: The police has no department in entomology. There is one person in the laboratory of Marseille, police laboratory, which besides its normal activities analysing vehicles and the soil has also part of that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Following on your answer, would it be correct to say that this institute in Rosny Sous Bois near Paris, I suppose there is no litigation about that, is it the institute who receives all requests for expertise?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Certainly. National police sees us for about 20 per cent of our dossiers, the rest is for the gendarmerie or the magistrates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Understood. The institute -- that you are the French specialists in your own field?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Are there other specialists in this -- on this subject, for instance, in the university in France?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: In France, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And in Europe?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: In Europe, yes, there are laboratories who tried to develop this activity or who already deal with these matters, but they are not police laboratories. They are either forensic institutes or universities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: According to your department of entomology, is it one of the units in Europe which works from morning until night, its your daily bread, if I may say, for all requests for expertise in entomology matters?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We are the only department in Europe who has an activity exclusively devoted to legal entomology or forensic entomology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. How many expertise did the department do since it was created?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Today, 717, and we do about 70 to 80 every year since the last three or four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And on these 70 and 80 post mortems done by your department every year, how many did you do yourself personally?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Depends on the years but it's between 12 and 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So in total, how many post mortems did you do in this field?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Since 2003, about 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Your institute in the entomology department, does it have research activities for its experiments?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Every year we have research programmes, applied research programmes to try to answer some problems which have been submitted to us during the year or during the year -- the years before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to give us an idea of the sort of research?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes. There is a lot of research on the biology of species with interesting for dates and there is a series of experiments on buried bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Buried bodies? I continue: Could you give us a little more details? What do you mean? What have you done? What are your results?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: We have buried in 2004, 21 sheep for a year. They stayed underground at different depths, minus 10, minus 30 and minus 90 centimetres and then we exhumed them and each time we got the entomology fauna and we analysed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I can therefore infer that there was an entomology fauna on these corpses?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Indeed, yes, certainly, after a year at 90 centimetres we did find this fauna.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I can see on your CV that you have written memorandum on post mortem interventions. I see that you are a member of an association, the European Association of Entomology, forensic entomology, which had a congress in London in 2004. Could you say a few words on this association and its goals?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: It's an association created in 2002 on the initiative of our own department, an association which groups all specialists of this matter -- in this field, whether police or university or forensic people, and it is -- the goal is to share data on fauna, which -- of interest -- which is of interest to us and we try to develop exchanges by the results between laboratories.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to pass to substantive questions, questions of substance, in general. Mr. Dourel, the Judges are particularly interested by Mrs. Lecomte's report of 15 June 2007 and the entomological aspects of this report. Mrs. Lecomte establishes a connection between the presence or the absence of larvae and the duration or presence of the bodies on the crime seat and possible interventions, manipulations, and in this connection, it seems that the entomological aspect is essential. You have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two things, if I may. It would be very helpful, I think, for those of us following if the pace could slow a little. And secondly, the comment that Mr. Dutertre made in the last line of the last question is a matter which in our submission requires to be explored with Professor Lecomte, in other words, the extent to which the entomological factors were essential to her conclusions rather than with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not to be excluded comments by this witness on what within his expertise seems to be important and not important. So it's not an area which could not be explored at all with this witness but at the same time I do agree with you that, of course, what the weight of certain elements is -- should -- could be commented by an outside observer but, of course, should be put first of all to the author of the report. [Interpretation] And Mr. Dutertre, could you please slow down because you are so fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've received also a request on my right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Dourel, you were asked to comment on Mrs. Lecomte's report. Your own report comports a general part and a specific part dedicated to the conclusions which Mrs. Lecomte gave on entomological matters, to summarise your own conclusions, as a specialist of this matter, you indicate at the end of your report - one can read this on document number 1985, 65 ter, at page 11 of the English version, but I will ask to be shown because this will be a bit faster - you indicate, and I will read this passage, "For the elements we have in our possession, concerning the elements we have in our possession, it appears that:" First subparagraph, "Since there was no entomological [Previous translation continued]... it was not possible to identify larvae belonging to the species of diptera, it was not possible to identify the larvae referred to as members of the diptera family. Second subparagraph, "Given the absence of samples from the bodies in their immediate environment and during autopsy operations and the absence of data on the environmental conditions prior to the discovery of the bodies, it is impossible, one, to establish a link between the presence of larvae and the time a body has been present, and two, it is impossible to establish a link between the presence or absence of larvae and the handling of a body." To be quite precise, I have added a little one and a little two to be quite clear in what I was reading. Now, this being said, Mr. Dourel, I would like to ask you a few questions in general and more specifically on the conclusions. First of all, principal questions, which have to do with entomology in general, the identification of insects and the sampling of larvae and the development of larvae. You indicate, and this can be seen on document 1985 in English page 5, and it can be found also -- you can see it on Sanction. It will be faster. You indicate therefore that those are specific smells during the different phases of alteration of the corpses. Those are the smells during the different phases of the body which attracts necrophagic species. I have two questions to ask on this to be quite sure I have understood. And so I would like to enlighten everybody on this. First question: If I do understand what you say there are several kind of insects who come to colonise a body with passing of time and each stage of the decomposition of a body corresponds one or several species of specific insects. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: My second question, is it therefore correct to say that from the entomological point of view, the identification of specimens present on the crime scene, at the crime scene, and also the determination of the stage of the specimen in question are essential inasmuch as each species reaches a given stage and has its own rhythm of evolution which enables to give an idea of the date of death, in particular. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. So the general mechanism of this matter being now clarified, I would go to the question of the identification of insects themselves. First question on this point is: Do you need a specific experience to distinguish on macroscopic experience, the larvae of different species?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In the department we have about a year of experience on the identification of immature species.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Talking about diptera only, can you tell us how many different species there are, sorts?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Diptera is a group, we don't know all of them, but on the necrophagic fauna, necrophagous, there are about 20 to 25 species.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it fair to say that a practice has developed in some cases according to which we have genetic analysis in order to determine a specific larva belongs to a type depending on the scene of crime?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: Yes. There are species that belong to the same family and they are very close to one -- to one another, and it's hard to identify them on the sole basis of morphological differences so we have to resort to DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. In this context if you do not have a collection of larvae that was collected on the spot and failing a detailed description of the larvae in an autopsy report, is it possible to indicate with accuracy what kind of larvae it is?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Let me now quote page 14 of Professor Lecomte's report. It is page 14 in French but page 13 in English. This is 65 ter list Exhibit, if I'm not mistaken, 1986. It's the second report. I'm sorry for not mentioning it. Yes, it is, indeed, the second report. First I'm going to quote the passage. This is body R-1, presence of dipterous larvae on the clothing and in the cranial cavity. This being said, can we show Exhibit P802, the first page, in English? This document is going to be on your screen in a few seconds. Sorry, it was page 2. Please zoom in on the first paragraph. I'll read it out to you: [In English] The body was dressed in clothes which were completely soaked in putrefied matter, soiled with earth, and covered by a mass of mobile cylindrical-shaped maggots about five to 20 centimetres long. [Interpretation] I guess there must be a mistake because apart from the film "Men in Black," I never happened to see any maggots that would be 20 centimetres long. But let us assume that we are dealing with millimetres. Now, on the basis of this description, Mr. Dourel, can you conclude that these are dipterous larvae, just as Mrs. Lecomte concluded?

utterances.speaker: LAURENT DOUREL
utterances.text: It is difficult to give a definite conclusion as to the presence of dipterous larvae. You must know that there are also other coleopterous larvae on body. They are white in appearance. They have legs, but they are very short and it's hard to see it with the naked eye.
